examples: I live on Juárez Street.
My car is red.
note: The Mexican word for a car (in Spain “coche”).

examples: Which bus goes downtown?
note: In Mexico “camión” mostly means a city bus.

examples: The store is on the corner.
We buy fruit at the market.
We're going downtown on Saturday.
The subway is near here.
Is the airport far?
The bank is across from the park.
We're going to the park with the kids.
The church is very old.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
Let's meet in the square.
note: The main square of a Mexican city is called “el zócalo”.

examples: The pharmacy is on the corner.
The subway is two blocks away.
note: In Mexico a “cuadra” = the stretch of street between two intersections.

examples: I live in a very quiet neighborhood.
note: In Mexico “colonia” = a neighborhood of a city.

examples: Turn right at the traffic light.
The store is to the right of the bank.
note: a la derecha = on the right, to the right.

examples: Turn left.
Keep going straight for two blocks.
I take the subway to go downtown.
Should we get a taxi?
Where is the subway station?
The pharmacy is open 24 hours.
The hospital is far from here.
Mexico City is huge.
note: La Ciudad de México (CDMX) = the capital of Mexico.

examples: My grandparents live in a small town.
There's a lot of traffic at this hour.
The parking lot is full.
Where is there an ATM?
Is there a pharmacy near here?
The hotel is over there.
note: allá = there (farther away); ahí = there (close by).

examples: The pharmacy is across from the park.
The bank is next to the hotel.
The parking lot is behind the building.
I live in a ten-story building.
Cross the bridge and turn right.
note: Colloquially also a long weekend: hacer puente.

examples: I live on an avenue with a lot of traffic.
Call the police.
note: el policía / la policía = also a police officer.

examples: What's your address?
At the traffic circle, take the second exit.
Walk on the sidewalk.
Let's meet in the main square.
note: What the main square of a city is called in Mexico.

examples: The best taquería is on the corner.

It's a very quiet neighborhood.
Safety is a problem in some areas.
This street is dangerous at night.
My street is very noisy.

note: Very Mexican: speed bumps are almost everywhere in Mexico.

examples: I take the minibus to go to work.
There was a huge traffic jam on the Periférico.

note: In Mexico City the boroughs are called alcaldías (formerly delegaciones).

We bought juice at a stall in the market.
note: Also: a job, a position (un puesto de trabajo).
